React Performance Optimization: Beyond useMemo and useCallback
entry.summary:
If you're optimizing a React app and your first instinct is to throw useMemo and useCallback everywhere—stop. That may not help, and might actually hurt performance. Let’s look at smarter, real-world strategies to make your React app faster and more responsive. Use the React DevTools Profiler to measure where your app slows down. 📌 Tip: Go to the "Profiler" tab in DevTools → Record interactions → Spot slow renders. Optimization without profiling is like treating a disease without a diagnosis. Deeply nested components re-render more than you think. Keep your tree shallow and split concerns: ✅ Good:
🚫 Bad:
3. Memoize Smartly (Not Blindly)
React.memo() is useful only if props don’t change frequently.
useCallback() prevents unnecessary re-creation of functions but comes with memory overhead.
useMemo() should be used only for expensive computations, not every function or array.
4. Code Split with Lazy Loading
For large apps, import components only when needed: const BlogPage = React.lazy(() => import('./pages/Blog')); }> For events like search inputs, use debounce: const debouncedSearch = useMemo(() => debounce(handleSearch, 300), []); Avoid unnecessary re-renders caused by changing references. Bad: Better: Final Thoughts Start by measuring. Then optimize where it actually matters. ✍️ Author: Cynthia Emeka
